specs.scene: Overhead flat-lay crowded to every edge: a printed enrollment roster with one name filled in above a column of blank ruled lines, a plain paper invoice with its total covered by a resting pen, a spiral notebook open to a page of dense handwriting, a stack of workbooks bound with twine, a black desktop calculator, a chipped ceramic mug half full of coffee, a small tin of index cards, a closed laptop pushed into the corner, and a coiled charging cable crossing the frame. Two bare hands enter from the bottom edge, one lifting the roster slightly, leaving small bare patches of plain desk between the objects.
specs.source_quote: Joanie Johnson runs Reframe and Ready, a cohort for clinicians navigating job loss

recognisable.why: Everyday office objects (mug, notebook, invoice) are familiar but the underlying business itself is not a known brand or trade.

legibility.why: House flat-lay style requires many overlapping objects, which works as gestalt texture but technically exceeds the one-or-two-element rule.

curiosity.why: The single filled line implies a small, possibly under-scale operation but does not state a clear verdict the viewer must resolve.

subject.why: No single anchor object dominates; the composition is deliberately distributed across many items.

credible.why: No figure is carried on the image, which scores full by rubric default.

stakes.why: The paperwork implies a real livelihood being built, but the stakes to the viewer are only mildly personal.

reexpress.why: The roster detail adds a concrete visual fact not present in any title wording, without restating a claim.

specs.overlay_big: A ROOM WITH AN END DATE
specs.scene: A documentary photograph of an empty meeting room in daylight: a round table surrounded by chairs pushed neatly against it, except for one chair pulled out and turned to face the camera at the table's near edge. The walls are plain and bare, the floor empty, and no other furniture interrupts the space.
specs.source_quote: It's a room with a start date and an end date

recognisable.why: A meeting room and chair are everyday objects but carry no brand or trade identity a cold viewer would name.

legibility.why: One pulled-out chair against a plain room reads as a single focal mass even at small size.

curiosity.why: The caption is a flat editorial verdict about impermanence that cannot be resolved by looking, matching the top-quartile pattern exactly.

subject.why: The single turned chair functions as a clear, if generic, object anchor.

credible.why: No figure appears anywhere on the frame.

stakes.why: The empty-room framing implies something ending or at risk, which touches the viewer's own sense of runway.

reexpress.why: The room metaphor reframes the episode's claim in visual terms none of the titles state directly.

specs.scene: A single spiral-bound workbook lies open on a plain wooden table, its blank cover facing up, pages slightly fanned by a light breeze. No hands, no other objects, and no surface markings interrupt the plain table around it.
specs.source_quote: The build risk is close to zero now

recognisable.why: A workbook is an ordinary, identifiable object, though it carries no brand or industry marker.

legibility.why: One object, plainly shown, resolves instantly as a single focal mass.

curiosity.why: Stating build risk is gone implies an unstated remaining risk, which the label deliberately does not resolve.

subject.why: The workbook is a single, distinctive anchor object of the trade.

credible.why: No figure is carried on the image.

stakes.why: The claim speaks directly to a viewer considering the same build, implying their own risk exposure.

reexpress.why: The overlay isolates one specific claim from the transcript that no title states, splitting the work cleanly.

specs.scene: A woman in plain clothing sits at a small desk in a home office, mid-motion as she writes on a paper notepad with a pen, phone held loosely in her other hand. The right half of the frame is clear plain wall, uncluttered, while she and the desk occupy the left half. No screen is visible on the desk.
specs.source_quote: That's the actual claim of this episode

recognisable.why: An unnamed individual with no public profile gives a cold viewer nothing recognisable to anchor on.

legibility.why: One person mid-action with a clear negative-space half resolves as a single focal mass.

curiosity.why: The phrase implies a verdict about legitimacy that the image alone cannot confirm or deny.

subject.why: A person captured mid-action is the strongest possible single anchor by rubric definition.

credible.why: No figure is carried on the image.

stakes.why: The scene implies personal stakes for anyone weighing whether their own small effort counts, but only moderately.

reexpress.why: The overlay interprets the episode's thesis rather than repeating any title's own wording.
